scenes.tts: A minister's son trained in Latin and Greek, Rose found an alphabet short one letter intolerable. He fed rats a fully synthetic diet of all nineteen then-known amino acids and watched them waste and die in the middle of plenty — proof that something essential was still missing.
scenes.visual: minister's son, alphabet one letter short; 19-amino-acid synthetic diet; rats waste and die; something missing
scenes.narration: A minister's son trained in Latin and Greek, Rose found an alphabet short one letter intolerable. He fed rats a fully synthetic diet of all nineteen then-known amino acids and watched them waste and die in the middle of plenty — proof that something essential was still missing.

scenes.tts: So he turned his Illinois lab into a fractionation works, grinding through milk protein by the kilogram to corner whatever casein held that corn protein lacked, and in 1935 his team crystallized it: threonine, named for its structural echo of the sugar threose.
scenes.visual: Illinois lab fractionation works; milk protein by the kilogram; casein vs corn protein; 1935 threonine; named for threose
scenes.narration: So he turned his Illinois lab into a fractionation works, grinding through milk protein by the kilogram to corner whatever casein held that corn protein lacked, and in 1935 his team crystallized it: threonine, named for its structural echo of the sugar threose.

scenes.tts: Then he moved the experiment onto healthy male graduate students, masking the sulfurous taste of the amino-acid mixture with a peppermint candy and pulling out one amino acid at a time to see which removals broke a grown human.
scenes.visual: healthy male graduate students; peppermint candy masks sulfurous mixture; remove one amino acid at a time
scenes.narration: Then he moved the experiment onto healthy male graduate students, masking the sulfurous taste of the amino-acid mixture with a peppermint candy and pulling out one amino acid at a time to see which removals broke a grown human.

scenes.tts: That patient subtraction is how we learned which amino acids an adult cannot live without and has to eat: Rose drew the line at eight, and histidine was added decades later to make the modern nine.
